drop0:08

drop6:02

Pack my bags and go." 4 · how (the next move)Trim the sung verse from 5:57-6:11 to a 3-second musical sting under the next work shot. 5 · rationaleThe channel typically loses 0.83% here; the jump to 1.77% tracks the length of the vocal interlude, not the content around it.
peak9:40
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises into the run-up to the reveal and holds for 35 samples (*+4.4% of viewers present, 4,810 regained*). 2 · evidence at that second“Say that you love” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)This is the sung bridge immediately before Emma announces the reveal: "Say that you love." 4 · how (the next move)Keep this 9-second musical run-in intact when re-editing the 12:50 interlude; it earns its length here because a reveal lands right after. 5 · rationaleMusic works when it bridges into a payoff, not when it replaces one — the contrast with 12:50 is the lesson.
peak9:49

drop12:50
1 · what the curve showedA late music-only interlude sheds viewers at 3.3x the channel's normal rate for this position (*6.8x the surrounding stop rate, 7,510 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“with this new color” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Narration ends on the color reveal payoff, then hands off to 25 seconds of song lyrics: "with this new color. Leaving in the morning." 4 · how (the next move)Cut 12:53-13:17 and rejoin on the next work beat, keeping music under narration rather than replacing it. 5 · rationaleThe payoff released viewers and the silent music bed gave them no reason to stay; 3.3x above channel norm confirms the interlude, not the position, is the leak.
peak14:30
1 · what the curve showedA short rewatch cluster on the outro reveal recap holds only 3 samples (*+3.3% of viewers present, 4,051 regained*). 2 · evidence at that second“more homey and more earthy” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Emma restates what she likes about the color choice: "more homey and more earthy." 4 · how (the next move)Move this 6-second color verdict to just before the 12:50 music interlude so viewers hear the judgment before the song starts. 5 · rationaleThe verdict is what viewers scrub back for; placing it where the current leak sits converts a rewatch into a reason to stay.

drop0:09
1 · what the curve showedThe greeting and week-recap opening bled viewers at 1.5x the channel's own rate for this spot (*4.3x the surrounding stop rate, 179,564 viewers, opening loss +14.6pp vs the channel median*). 2 · evidence at that second“Hi friends and welcome back” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Emma opens with a housekeeping recap before any promise lands: "Hi friends and welcome back to my channel." Then teases next week's paint, not this week's payoff. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 0:09-0:31 and open on the 7:29 "Oh my gosh, this is awful" panic, then cut back to what she is trying to build. 5 · rationaleBy 1:00 this video holds 44.5% vs a channel median of 61.0% (beats 3 of 103) — the loss is locked in during this recap, not later.
drop3:18
1 · what the curve showedA silent music-only stretch quit at 2.0x the channel's rate here (*4.2x the surrounding stop rate, 9,638 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“Two down. Well, three down total” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The transcript is almost entirely "[music]" from 2:49 to 3:37 with one flat line: "Two down. Well, three down total." No new information enters for nearly 20 seconds. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 3:17-3:37 down to a 4-second time-lapse and overlay a specific stake — cuts remaining, or what goes wrong if this one is off. 5 · rationaleThe stop rate doubles the channel norm at a spot where nothing is being said or shown to advance the build.
drop7:59
1 · what the curve showedThe sponsor read for Tester Up lost viewers at 6.8x the channel's typical rate for this spot, the sharpest anomaly in the video (*31.3x the surrounding stop rate, 40,584 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“sponsor of today's episode” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The read pivots straight out of a panic beat into an ad: "you would love Tester Up, who is the sponsor of today's episode" — the tension the viewer was watching for is released before the ad, not held through it. 4 · how (the next move)Trial moving this read to 7:38 mid-panic — cut in on "What am I doing? I don't think I can do this" — run Tester Up while the outcome is unresolved, then deliver the fix at 9:11. 5 · rationaleAds hold best at the height of anticipation; releasing the beat first ("let's get back to work") is exactly when viewers feel licensed to leave. cautionVerify with Tester Up that a mid-tension placement satisfies the sponsor contract; success shows as stopRate here falling toward the 0.96% channel norm.
peak9:01
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbed and held for 47 samples right as the sponsor ended and the fix landed (*+9.9% of viewers present, 14,290 regained, holding 23.4%*). 2 · evidence at that second“I fixed it, but let's just say” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers scrubbed back to hear the resolution of the panic beat: "I fixed it, but let's just say the cuts were not perfect" — the answer to the 7:33 "this is awful" moment. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a 6-second cold-open teaser of this fix reveal before 0:09, cutting directly from "I fixed it" back to the start of the build. 5 · rationaleThe rewind proves viewers care about the recovery, not the recap — putting the recovery near the top is what the opening minute is missing.
peak9:12
1 · what the curve showedA second replay peak stacked on the same recovery segment, 11 seconds after the first (*+4.7% of viewers present, 7,485 regained, holding 24.5%*). 2 · evidence at that second“I had to chisel these a little bit” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewound again to see the specific damage explained: "I had to chisel these a little bit, but I did end up getting it" — the how, right after the what. 4 · how (the next move)Merge 9:11-9:40 into a single tight explainer with an on-screen close-up of the beveled piece and the chisel fix — do not let this beat drift. 5 · rationaleTwo stacked rewinds on the same fix mean the segment is doing the work; making it visually clearer removes the need to rewind and keeps the audience moving forward.
peak14:14
1 · what the curve showedAudience rose and held for 17 samples on the milestone that all cuts were finished (*+5.1% of viewers present, 8,166 regained, holding 24.9%*). 2 · evidence at that second“cuts are done. I can't believe it” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rewind sits on the explicit payoff line: "cuts are done. I can't believe it" — the first clean resolution of the project's central struggle. 4 · how (the next move)Show the finished-cuts reveal in the thumbnail-adjacent first 15 seconds as a flash-forward, then return to 0:32 to start the build. 5 · rationaleViewers scrubbed back specifically for this milestone, so it is the reward the opening should be promising rather than "finishing modifying the window sashes".

drop0:09
1 · what the curve showedThe opening 20 seconds actually hold better than the channel usually does here (*7.04% stop rate, 0.7x the channel norm, 30,629 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“I was in Alabama working” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Standard channel greeting and week-off recap: "Hi friends and welcome back" then "I was in Alabama working with a music producer". 4 · how (the next move)Keep the current open — it beats the channel's intro average by 4pp (17.9% vs 21.9%) and no surgery is warranted. 5 · rationaleJoos: intros should deliver context and stakes fast, and this one already outperforms cohort — changing it risks the lead this video builds by 2:00.
drop2:16
1 · what the curve showedA 10-second gap holds better than the channel typically does here (*0.51% stop rate, 0.4x channel norm, 8,569 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“let's do it” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The transcript shows a work-transition beat: "let's do it" then 27 seconds of silent priming setup before "I have the primer here". 4 · how (the next move)Leave as-is — this moment beats the channel's habit at this timestamp by more than half. 5 · rationaleThe spikeRatio flags it against the immediate preceding stretch, but vs the channel it under-loses; acting here would trade a real strength for cosmetic smoothing.
drop3:24
1 · what the curve showedA 39-second music-only montage loses viewers at twice the channel's rate for this position (*2.53% stop rate, 2.0x channel norm, 10,187 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“play some music so that you don't” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Dialogue stops at "play some music so that you don't have to listen to the fan" and 27 seconds of licensed song play with no narration or progression. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 3:15-3:38 down to a 6-8 second time-lapse with an on-screen progress caption, rejoining on "So really is quite a massive gap". 5 · rationaleJoos: pacing is the flow of NEW information — something should change every ~5 seconds, and a silent music bed with no visible progression flattens that flow.
drop6:39
1 · what the curve showedThe sponsor pivot drops the audience from 49.1% to 36.8%, a channel-anomalous loss (*6.19% stop rate, 5.2x channel norm, 29,389 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“The outside is done” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The read opens on the sponsor's name after a completed exterior beat: "The outside is done" then straight into "Sundays for Dogs reached out". 4 · how (the next move)Rebuild this read like "Addressing The Truth." at 5:27 (0.0% loss); open on the dogs eating from the garden, defer brand name until after the hook. 5 · rationalePlaybook: never open with "sponsored by", and never place an ad right after a payoff — the exterior reveal at 6:32 released viewers before the pitch landed. cautionConfirm the brand contract permits reordering the opening line; if locked, cross-cut the read with the interior work instead.
peak6:39
1 · what the curve showedA brief 1-sample uptick precedes the sponsor drop (*3.2% rise, 4,284 viewers, 45th percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“The outside is done” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rise lands on "The outside is done" — viewers scrubbing back to catch the exterior completion beat before the ad break. 4 · how (the next move)Hold this exterior payoff for 3-4 more seconds with a wide shot before the sponsor pivot, giving the moment room to land. 5 · rationaleThe peak sits exactly where the 6:39 drop starts — viewers wanted more of the payoff and got the ad instead, which the sponsor fix above already addresses.
peak7:47
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbs 7.8% of those present and holds for 52 samples (*8,710 viewers regained, 60th percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“let's get back to work” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind past the sponsor CTA "use my code Emma for 30% off" to reach "let's get back to work" and the returning music bed. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load the "back to work" cue to 7:36 and shorten the CTA tail; the rewind proves viewers are hunting for the work resumption. 5 · rationaleJoos: replay peaks flag the exact moment viewers want to reach — moving it earlier lets more of the 36.8% who stayed after 6:39 find it without scrubbing.
peak7:56
1 · what the curve showedA second replay bump lands 9 seconds later, holding 13 samples (*4.9% rise, 5,891 viewers, 61st percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“you're speaking is gold” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The transcript here is pure song: "Tell me what you're feeling. Every single you're speaking is gold" — viewers are rewinding into the music-and-painting montage. 4 · how (the next move)Extend this montage by 5-8 seconds and lift the same song cue into the 9:53 valley to carry that weaker moment. 5 · rationaleJoos: a peak that earns rewinds is an asset — reusing its audio signature at a nearby valley borrows the anticipation the audience already showed for it. cautionCheck music-license terms allow reusing the cue at 9:53 within the same video.
drop9:24
1 · what the curve showedA 10-second beat around the second-frame reset loses viewers at the channel's normal rate (*0.93% stop rate, 1.0x channel norm, 4,870 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“tag me in your story” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A tag-me-on-Instagram aside interrupts the work: "tag me in your story, post a picture or video of you guys watching". 4 · how (the next move)Trial moving the Instagram ask into the outro after 15:48; measure whether the 9:24 stopRate drops toward the 0.5% floor the video hits elsewhere. 5 · rationaleJoos: pattern interrupts belong in valleys, not before a fresh work segment — the ask here breaks momentum right before "let's get on to the second frame". cautionConfirm the ask isn't contractually placed mid-video; if so, cut it to one sentence rather than moving it.
drop9:53
1 · what the curve showedA 19-second music-only montage during the second-frame paint loses viewers at 2.4x the channel norm here (*1.85% stop rate, 5,019 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“the most satisfying part, the paint” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)After "the most satisfying part, the paint" the audio drops to song lyrics with no VO or progress marker for nearly 20 seconds. 4 · how (the next move)Trim 9:45-10:12 to 8 seconds and overlay a coat-count or timer caption, rejoining on the next spoken beat. 5 · rationaleJoos: strip-down/repetition kills retention — a second music-bed after the 3:24 one teaches the audience the video pauses whenever the song starts.
drop12:19
1 · what the curve showedThe third-window transition loses viewers at over twice the channel's rate for reveals (*1.73% stop rate, 2.1x channel norm, 6,847 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“take a look at the before and after” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The moment teases a reveal without delivering it: "take a look at the before and after" is promised, then "Let's move on to the third window" and a music-only stretch. 4 · how (the next move)Trial cutting 12:06-12:18 and delivering the before/after Emma just promised, before starting window three; watch for stopRate at 12:19 dropping below 1.0%. 5 · rationaleJoos: reveals dominate this channel's cohort (average +0.2% gain) and this one lost 2.6% instead — the promised payoff was deferred, releasing anticipation. cautionVerify the before/after footage exists at this stage; if only the final reveal exists, tighten the music bed to 4 seconds instead.
peak14:45

drop15:23

This one under-signals and holds; the 15:23 stopRate ticking up matches the channel's baseline for this position.

drop0:45

peak5:01

1 · what the curve showedAudience climbs and stays up for seventeen straight samples, unusually sustained (*+8.8% of the room, 160 viewers regained, 84th percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“i would see woods like that” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rewind target is the manifestation thesis stated cleanly: "i knew that someday i would see woods like that". 4 · how (the next move)Move this line into the first 30 seconds so the opening states the manifestation stake before the coyote reveal earns it. 5 · rationaleThe intro's job is context plus stakes plus goal fast; the audience is voting that this sentence is the real stake of the video. cautionConfirm the line still reads as setup once removed from its current placement — if it needs the woods visual, pair it with that shot.
peak10:28
1 · what the curve showedThe audience swells into the coyote moment and holds through it (*+17.2% of the room, 337 viewers regained, held 7 samples, 88th percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“i haven't seen any coyotes” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers are scrubbing back into the manifestation-to-coyote sequence: "i haven't seen any coyotes" landing seconds before she sees one. 4 · how (the next move)Cut a 30-second standalone clip from 9:59 to 10:36 and pin it as the channel trailer or a Short titled around the manifestation-then-coyote beat. 5 · rationaleA reveal that earns rewinds is an asset; surfacing it outside the video mines demand the retention curve is already proving.
drop10:36
1 · what the curve showedThe coyote sighting triggers the video's sharpest exit even as others rewind to it (*15.8x surrounding stop rate, 3.1x channel norm, 242 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“holy freak okay holy freaking” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The payoff lands and immediately dissipates into repeated exclamations: "holy freak" then "holy freaking" then "that was a big dog". 4 · how (the next move)Cut 10:40-10:48 and jump straight to "there were dogs chasing it" so the reveal keeps escalating instead of deflating. 5 · rationaleRetention drops the moment tension is spent; compressing the aftermath keeps the narrative question (what happens to Nigel) live.
peak10:36
1 · what the curve showedOne-sample tick coinciding with the coyote sighting itself (*+5.8% of the room, 134 viewers regained, held 1 sample, 89th percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“holy sh i just saw a coyote” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Same rewind target as the sustained peak above: viewers landing on "holy sh i just saw a coyote" to catch the moment of realization. 4 · how (the next move)Hold the coyote frame an extra beat with a riser starting at 10:16 so the payoff feels earned rather than accidental. 5 · rationaleAnticipatory risers about twenty seconds before a key moment flatten retention through the buildup and hold more of the room to the payoff. cautionSingle-sample ticks can be artifacts — treat this as confirmation of the 10:28 sustained peak, not an independent signal.

curve100 samples, stored one per percent runtime19:25 gone by 0:3029.3% at halfway41% still watching methodhazard = (present before − present after) ÷ present before at each moment; baseline = mean hazard of the previous 5 moments, floored; flagged when the excess viewers lost beyond baseline ranks high; a rise is a rewind only when no comparable drop precedes it and the lift survives the next sample

Red marks are flagged drops, green are earned rewinds. Hover a mark for its note.

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:12
1 · what the curve showedThe first-frame music-and-title cold open sheds 17 points of the audience between 0:12 and 0:23 (*9.8x spike, 86 viewers, 98.2% to 80.9%*). 2 · evidence at that second“more than you thought” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The opening is wordless music and applause with only the muttered fragment before any premise lands. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 0:12-0:23 of music and drop in a 6-second before/after van cutaway with a spoken promise of what gets built. 5 · rationaleThis channel's median holds 92.7% at 0:15 and this video is already at 98.2%; the loss lands on the silent stretch, not the click.
drop8:44
1 · what the curve showedA wordless music bridge at 8:44-8:56 loses 2.9 points (*13.2x spike, 2.0x this channel's norm here, 15 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“[8:46] [Music]” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Eight seconds of music and a single sung syllable sit between two build segments before the next-day voiceover picks up. 4 · how (the next move)Trim 8:44-8:56 to a 3-second cut and lay the 9:01 blackout-window voiceover over the tail so the next beat starts sooner. 5 · rationaleThe channel typically loses under 1% at this position; the doubling comes from dead air, not the content on either side.
peak12:49
1 · what the curve showedThe audience rises 6.6% and holds for five samples across 12:49 (*14 viewers regained, sitting at 40.4%*). 2 · evidence at that second“it feels like you're backing away” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers are rewinding into the sung bridge that runs from 12:36 through the flooring transition at 13:11. 4 · how (the next move)Credit the track in the description at this timestamp and keep the bridge intact in any re-edit. 5 · rationaleTwo of the three replay peaks cluster on this same music bed, so the song itself is pulling scrubs, not the build content around it.
peak13:01
1 · what the curve showedThe audience climbs 10.1% right before the flooring reveal and holds for two samples (*23 viewers regained, sitting at 44.5%*). 2 · evidence at that second“okay so i am working on the flooring now” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers are scrubbing back into the music-and-vocal bridge that immediately precedes her sitting down to explain the finished floor. 4 · how (the next move)Cut a 30-second standalone flooring short from 13:11-13:42 and pin it as a chapter marker on this video. 5 · rationaleThe rewind lands on the setup for the DIY flooring explainer, so isolating that beat gives returning viewers a direct route in.
drop13:12
1 · what the curve showedA flooring segue at 13:12-13:36 loses 5.8 points in 23 seconds (*17.7x the surrounding stop rate, 4.8x this channel's norm here, 27 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“it's hard but it's not that hard” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A music bed with the vocal fragment cuts abruptly into a mid-thought explainer that opens with a hedge before any visible progress. 4 · how (the next move)Cut the music tail 13:07-13:14 and start the segment on the finished-floor reveal, then let her explain how she got there. 5 · rationaleThe channel typically loses 0.55% here; this moment runs 2.66%, so the cost is the transition itself, not the flooring content.
peak18:50
1 · what the curve showedThe audience rises 6.8% in the final minute and holds through the end (*14 viewers regained, ending at 40.9%*). 2 · evidence at that second“[18:46] call me” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The closing montage runs music, applause and a sung line with no wrap-up talk, so viewers rewind the finished-build reveal instead of leaving. 4 · how (the next move)Hold this outro structure and add a 3-second on-screen cut list at 19:10 so returning viewers see what was built. 5 · rationaleThis video ranks 29 of 104 on end-hold versus 52 of 104 at halfway; the silent finish is doing real work and should not be talked over.

VAN LIFE | I Bought A Van! » Living in a Van Vlog

published 2020-11-18 · analysed 2026-08-26

1 · Retention breakdown

curve100 samples, stored one per percent runtime18:31 gone by 0:3045.4% at halfway25% still watching methodhazard = (present before − present after) ÷ present before at each moment; baseline = mean hazard of the previous 5 moments, floored; flagged when the excess viewers lost beyond baseline ranks high; a rise is a rewind only when no comparable drop precedes it and the lift survives the next sample

Red marks are flagged drops, green are earned rewinds. Hover a mark for its note.

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:10
1 · what the curve showedThe opening 23 seconds shed nearly half the room, running almost twice the channel's usual intro loss (*17.50% stop rate, 1.9x channel norm, 4,330 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“this one isn't even really the perfect one” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The video opens with a greeting and a hedged tease — "i might be buying a van tomorrow" followed by admitting "this one isn't even really the perfect one" — undercutting the title's promise. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 0:10-0:38 and open on the 3:03 "it's a done deal" reveal, then flash back to the search. 5 · rationaleJoos: never restate the premise the thumbnail sold, and never open on a greeting — lead with the strong-emotion moment the audience is already rewinding to.
peak2:24
1 · what the curve showedAudience rose 9.5 points and held for thirteen samples, the longest sustained lift in the video (*+446 viewers regained, audience reaches 30.3%*). 2 · evidence at that second“road trip with me to california” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers are rewinding the road-trip plan reveal — "another month here until my sister can get two weeks off of work to take the road trip with me to california." 4 · how (the next move)Tease "California road trip with my sister" in the first 30 seconds as an unresolved stake for the video. 5 · rationaleJoos: keep the narrative suspense layer live across the whole video — a concrete future stake, teased early, holds the middle that currently sags to 25.4%.
peak2:36
1 · what the curve showedAudience rose 6.7 points and held for nine samples in the 67th percentile against similar videos (*+344 viewers regained, audience reaches 32.3%*). 2 · evidence at that second“very cool i think that's everything” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers replay the "very cool i think that's everything" beat that immediately precedes the purchase — the pre-reveal buildup itself is holding. 4 · how (the next move)Trial a 20-second riser under 2:32-3:03 to extend anticipation into the reveal, and A/B against the current cut. 5 · rationaleJoos: start anticipatory risers ~20 seconds before a key moment — retention flattens through the buildup, and this stretch already proves the audience wants more of it. cautionThe riser must not signal an outro or resolve the tension early — measure success by whether the 3:00-3:30 window holds above 33% audience.
peak2:47
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbed 8.7 points and held for six samples, sitting in the 71st percentile against similar videos (*+480 viewers regained, audience reaches 35.1%*). 2 · evidence at that second“it's a done deal it's a done deal” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers are rewinding to the "it's a done deal it's a done deal i can't believe it" moment — the actual purchase reveal the title promised. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load this exact line into the first 10 seconds as the cold open, then cut back to the search. 5 · rationaleJoos: a reveal that earns rewinds is an asset — tease it early and structure toward it, because the intro currently buries what the audience most wants.
drop3:09
1 · what the curve showedA 33-second stretch loses viewers at exactly the channel's usual rate for this position (*2.07% stop rate, 1.0x channel norm, 489 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“maybe we should go to walmart first” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The purchase beat resolves into a mundane errands segue — "maybe we should go to walmart first" for a "steering wheel cover" — releasing tension right after the reveal. 4 · how (the next move)Move the Walmart errand to a montage after 4:00 and cut straight from 3:09 into driving the van away. 5 · rationaleJoos: never place a flat beat right after a payoff — viewers feel released and leave; the reveal at 3:03 is the peak, protect it with continued momentum.
drop14:49
1 · what the curve showedA 33-second lull loses a fifth of the remaining room at nearly five times the channel's usual rate here (*7.20% stop rate, 13.3x spike, 892 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“it's so rare that i feel this good” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The creator stops the action to monologue about feelings — "i just want to say again how good i feel" and "it's so rare that i feel this good" — with no new information landing. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 14:39-15:22 entirely and rejoin on the next visible change inside the van. 5 · rationaleJoos: pacing is the flow of NEW information — something should visibly change every ~5 seconds, and repeated feelings-talk is exactly the repetition to kill.
